## Zoning & Development Analysis: 1601 N Milwaukee Ave (PIN 14313320180000)

**Parcel resolution: authoritative** — the PIN is confirmed from Cook County address records, so all parcel-level data below describes this specific property.

---

### 1. Zoning District

This parcel is zoned **B3-2** (Community Shopping District, Density 2). The classification comes from the City's official GIS system (Ordinance No. 17230). You can verify it on the [Chicago Zoning Map](https://gisapps.chicago.gov/ZoningMapWeb/?liab=1&config=zoning).

The B3 district is intended for a broad range of retail and service uses, often in larger buildings or shopping-center formats, with development that tends to be destination-oriented and accommodates some use types not permitted in B1 or B2 [1]. The "-2" suffix sets the bulk/density tier (see item 3).

---

### 2. Ground-Floor Retail with Apartments Above

**Yes, this is permitted by-right.** In B3 districts:

- **Dwelling units located above the ground floor**: Permitted by-right ("P") [3]
- **Retail/commercial uses on the ground floor**: Permitted by-right in B3 [1]

So a mixed-use building with ground-floor commercial and residential above is straightforwardly allowed in B3-2 without a special use or planned development approval — subject to bulk standards and the overlays discussed below.

> *Note:* Artist live/work space on the ground floor requires special use approval ("S") in B3 [3].

---

### 3. Key Bulk and Density Standards

The context does not include the full B3-2 bulk table (`zone_definition` was not returned), so I can confirm the **applicable framework** from the code but cannot state every precise numeric limit from this query alone. Here is what can be confirmed:

**Floor Area Ratio (FAR)**
All B and C district development is subject to maximum FAR standards set by table under [5]. For B3-2, the base FAR is set by the dash-2 tier. **A FAR increase for transit-served locations** is available — but only in **dash-3** districts (B1-3, B2-3, B3-3, etc.) via Type 1 map amendment, planned development, or ARO entitlement [5]. This parcel is B3-**2**, so the FAR bonus does **not** apply here by right.

**Height, Lot Coverage, Setbacks**
These are governed by the B3-2 bulk table in [5] and cross-referenced provisions. The context did not return the specific numeric values for B3-2 (stories, feet, lot area per unit). You should consult the full table at Chicago Municipal Code § 17-3-0400 directly. The City's [Zoning Map](https://gisapps.chicago.gov/ZoningMapWeb/?liab=1&config=zoning) and the Department of Planning & Development's Zoning desk (312-744-5777) can provide the precise numbers.

**Residential Density (Lot Area per Dwelling Unit)**
Ground-floor residential conversion is handled under a special exception: the Zoning Administrator may approve conversion of a vacant or occupied commercial space below the second floor into residential units under [5] (§ 17-3-0402-C). Above-grade units are subject to the B3-2 lot-area-per-unit standard in the bulk table.

*What I could not determine:* The exact numeric FAR cap, maximum height in feet/stories, minimum lot area per dwelling unit, and front/rear setback requirements for B3-2 — the bulk table was not returned in this query. These are critical numbers to obtain before designing any project.

---

### 4. Overlays and Special Designations

This parcel carries **multiple significant overlays**:

- **🏛 Individual Landmark Building** — The property is flagged as an individual Chicago landmark (CHRS survey rating: "orange"; historic name: **Noel State Bank**). This is the most consequential overlay: exterior alterations, demolition, or significant rehabilitation require review and approval by the **Commission on Chicago Landmarks**. This applies regardless of base zoning.

- **🏘 Milwaukee Avenue Historic District** — The parcel sits within a local Chicago historic district. District-level design standards apply to exterior changes.

- **📜 Wicker Park Historic District (National Register)** — Also listed on the National Register of Historic Places. While National Register listing does not impose local regulatory restrictions by itself, it signals potential eligibility for **federal and state historic tax credits** (20% federal / 25% Illinois) if the rehabilitation meets the Secretary of the Interior's Standards. Verify at the Illinois Historic Preservation Agency.

- **🚇 Transit-Oriented Development (CTA)** — The parcel is in a CTA TOD overlay (Damen Blue Line station is just 0.07 miles away). See parking discussion in item 5.

- **🏠 ADU Eligible Area** — Accessory Dwelling Units are permitted under Chicago's ADU ordinance. This expands options for adding a coach house or in-unit conversion.

- **📋 Affordable Requirements Ordinance (ARO) Zone** — Any residential project requiring a zoning entitlement (map amendment, special use, or planned development) that produces 10 or more units triggers ARO obligations. West Town has 20 ARO housing projects totaling 291 affordable units in the community area. Verify current ARO thresholds with the Department of Housing.

- **🏪 Wicker Park Special Service Area (SSA)** — The parcel is within the Wicker Park SSA. An additional SSA levy appears in the tax bill (City of Chicago Special Service Area 33: ~$2,363/year). SSA membership may also involve facade and streetscape standards; check with the SSA administrator.

- **No Planned Development** — The parcel is not currently in a planned development, though one may be required for large projects (see item 6).

- **No Lakefront Protection, No PMD, No Special District** (industrial or otherwise).

---

### 5. Parking Requirement and Transit Reduction

**Transit-served parking relief is available.** Because the parcel is within the CTA TOD overlay (Damen Blue Line, 0.07 mi), the minimum parking requirement can be **reduced up to 100%** under § 17-10-0102-B — meaning a project here could potentially build with **zero required parking spaces**. This relief applies by right; no Type 1 amendment or planned development is needed for the parking reduction alone.

> ⚠️ **Important caveat:** This is a B3-**2** district. The FAR/density bonus available in dash-3 districts does **not** apply here. The parking relief is the transit benefit; no density, FAR, or height bonus is available at B3-2 [as confirmed by `tod_benefits`].

Standard B3-2 parking ratios for residential units are set in § 17-10-0207-C [3] and commercial uses in § 17-10-0200 et seq. Verify the base ratios with the Zoning desk before claiming any reduction.

---

### 6. Demolition and New Mixed-Use Construction: Approvals and Restrictions

**This is where the landmark designation becomes the dominant constraint.**

#### Landmark / Historic Review
Because this building is an **individual Chicago landmark** (Noel State Bank), demolition faces an extraordinarily high bar. Under Chicago's landmarks ordinance, demolition of a landmark building requires Commission on Chicago Landmarks approval and City Council concurrence — it is rarely granted absent demonstrated economic hardship. Similarly, exterior alterations and new construction on a landmark site must be reviewed for consistency with the landmark's character-defining features.

*Being on the National Register also means that federal undertakings (e.g., federally backed financing) trigger Section 106 review under the National Historic Preservation Act.*

#### Zoning / Scale Thresholds
Even setting aside landmark constraints, new construction at this scale may trigger **mandatory planned development** thresholds under § 17-8-0500, depending on the proposed building's height, floor area, and unit count [2], [5]. Check those thresholds early — exceeding them requires a full PD process before the Chicago Plan Commission.

#### What Approvals Would Be Required (at minimum):
1. **Commission on Chicago Landmarks** — demolition or exterior alteration approval (likely the hardest hurdle)
